creator: MJB ADHD
provenance: Original coded vector layouts and wording; no third-party meme artwork

cards.title: One useful tab
cards.caption: One question can turn into several detours. This is a relatable exaggeration, not a diagnostic example.
cards.alt: Original two-panel meme: one browser tab becomes many tabs. Text: Me: One useful tab. The tabs: We invited friends.

cards.title: The missing start button
cards.caption: Wanting to act and getting started can feel very different. The image illustrates an experience, not a proven mechanism.
cards.alt: Original two-panel meme: a clear task plan beside a waiting start button. Text: The plan: Start the thing. The start button: Please wait.

cards.title: Just two minutes
cards.caption: A joke about losing track of time while absorbed. Experiences vary, and this image cannot identify ADHD.
cards.alt: Original two-panel meme: a clock labelled 10:00 becomes 12:00. Text: Me: Just two minutes. Time: That was a suggestion.

cards.title: I will remember that
cards.caption: A joke about losing an intention before acting on it. An external note can keep the next action visible; recognising the joke is not a diagnosis.
cards.alt: Original two-panel meme: a note labelled Remember this, then an empty note with a question mark. Text: Me: I will remember that. Brain: Remember what?

cards.title: Somewhere very safe
cards.caption: A relatable exaggeration about misplaced objects. A consistent visible home for an item can reduce searching; this experience is not unique to ADHD.
cards.alt: Original two-panel meme: a key placed in a box, then three identical boxes marked with question marks. Text: Me: It is somewhere safe. Somewhere safe: Classified.

cards.title: Almost finished
cards.caption: A joke about a fresh idea interrupting completion. Keeping an ideas list beside the current task can preserve the idea without losing the next step.
cards.alt: Original two-panel meme: a progress bar nearly full, then a bright new idea next to an unfinished bar. Text: Task: Almost finished. Brain: New idea unlocked.

cards.title: All channels selected
cards.caption: An illustration of feeling overloaded by competing inputs. Sensory experiences vary and can have many explanations; this is not a diagnostic example.
cards.alt: Original two-panel meme: one active sound slider, then six active sliders. Text: Room: Just background noise. Brain: All channels selected.

cards.title: Explain briefly
cards.caption: A joke about fitting a complicated experience into a small form. Lead with the decision needed, then provide the supporting chronology.
cards.alt: Original two-panel meme: a small form with three lines, then a row of dated timeline cards. Text: Form: Explain it briefly. Me: Opens the full timeline.

cards.title: The first step
cards.top: PLAN: One step at a time.
cards.caption: Planning can become a task of its own. A small concrete next action can make the starting point clearer; the image is a joke, not a mechanism claim.
cards.alt: Original two-panel meme: one step marked Start, then a large staircase of planning steps. Text: Plan: One step at a time. Me: Builds a staircase first.
